I changed `ndarray_to_mgr` in `pandas/core/internals/construction.py` so the workload makes one copy of the array instead of two.

Before, `DataFrame(arr, dtype="int32", copy=True)` copied the float32 array first, then converted it to int32, which copies again. Now the first copy is skipped when the input is a numeric or bool ndarray and the conversion to a different numeric or bool dtype follows. That conversion already produces a fresh array. All other inputs behave as before.

I ran a quick check on the workload's call. The result is int32 and doesn't share memory with the input, so the copy semantics hold. It now takes about 0.65 ms per call over 100 runs. I didn't time the original code, so I can't give a before/after figure. I didn't run the 1,000-repeat script or any pytest files.
